title: the explorer's /help takes its name column from its longest section heading, so every meaning starts far right and is cut at ordinary widths
body:
Found by ic on 2026-09-24 in the 3.2.1 doc audit, driven in a pty on the pair at `4c687eaad`.

Seen: in the explorer's `/help`, every meaning starts near column 72 in a 110-column terminal, and the longer ones are cut with `…` -- eg "cross between the fields and the pane…" and "search the index -- the hits open in …". At 100 columns the meaning column is narrower still.

Mechanism, read by ic at HEAD: `help.rs:52-54` builds a section heading as an ordinary row, `Row::new(text, "", "label")`, so the heading's text sits in the NAME column, and `layout.rs:1080-1091` `plan()` sets `name_width` to the longest title of all the rows, capped only by `width - GAP - MIN_VALUE_COLS`. So the longest heading -- "intent commands -- run one with /<name>, /help <name> for its own page", drawn at `help.rs:250` -- sets the name column for every row. A likely fix is to leave heading rows out of the longest-name measure; the fixer names the mechanism.

Why it matters: the new explorer guide, `docs/explorer.md`, names `/help` as the authority for keys and commands, because a hand-written keymap would be a second home that goes stale, and it shows a shot of `/help`. A reader it sends there at an ordinary width cannot read most of the meanings.

Disposition: hv's, asked on 2026-09-24. It is outside the shipping-grade class of hv decision 33 (1). vc recommends it ride 3.2.1 as a named exception, stacked on the register landing's judging run so it costs no run of its own, because the guide sends every reader to this screen.
